subject: Data handling: retention scope and exception options (post-call recap)
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Holt <sarah.holt@healtech.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 16:23:00 -0800
Subject: Data handling: retention scope and exception options (post-call recap)

Hi Sarah — great to speak earlier. Quick recap from our discovery and proposed next steps so we have alignment for legal/security: 

What we heard (HealTech requirements)
- No permanent retention of raw transcripts containing PII for clinical flows — preferred: 0-retention for PII by default.
- Audit logs and metrics required for incident investigations, but HealTech prefers a short window (24–72 hrs) unless an incident opens.
- Data residency: production inference must run in us-west for US patient data.
- Evidence needed: SOC 2 summary + DPA with explicit retention carve-outs and logging controls

Redwood options we discussed
- Zero-retention mode: ephemeral session handling and no token-level logs for designated routes (can be scoped per API key or model route).
- Shortened logs: default token and request logs kept 24–72 hrs; configurable per-route in Dedicated or Private.
- Custom retention schedule: we can propose route-based TTLs (e.g., transcripts=0, kv-cache=7d, debug-logs=48h) and add an exceptions clause in the DPA.

Open questions / decisions needed from HealTech
1) Is 0-retention mandatory for all transcripts or only for flows that include PHI/PII?
2) Do you require any aggregated analytics to be retained beyond 72 hrs for product telemetry?
3) Legal: preferred language for retention carve-outs and SLA expectations?

Suggested next steps
- Marcus to share SOC 2 summary and a DPA redline that includes a sample route-based retention matrix (see attachments and Marcus' note).
- HealTech legal to flag required redline changes and confirm whether 0-retention must be absolute or scoped.
- Schedule 30-min follow-up with security/legal (suggest Thurs 2/12).

Thanks — I’ll mark action items and follow up with the attachments.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0187

Attachments referenced: SOC2-summary.pdf (summary), DPA-proposed-redline.docx (initial proposal)
From: Sarah Holt <sarah.holt@healtech.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: HealTech Legal <legal@healtech.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Data handling: retention scope and exception options (post-call recap)

Thanks for the clear recap, Olga — helpful. A few clarifications from our side before we loop legal fully: 

- 0-retention: HealTech's security team strongly prefers 0-retention for any transcript that contains patient-identifiable information. For non-PII chat transcripts used purely for product analytics, we could accept a short retention window (24–72h). So we need the DPA to support per-route scoping (we can tag sensitive routes).

- Logs/metrics: we do need short-lived audit logs for troubleshooting and incident timelines, but we want them purged within 48 hours unless an incident is declared. Will Redwood support on-demand preservation if we need to retain for an investigation?

- Evidence: please send SOC 2 summary and the DPA redline. Also, does Redwood offer an option to host inference in our VPC (private deployment) as an alternative if the DPA changes are not accepted? That may be required for certain sub-projects.

If you can send the docs, I will schedule a legal/security sync for Thurs 2/12 at 11:00am ET — I’ll include our CISO and procurement.

--
Sarah Holt
Head of Integrations, HealTech
sarah.holt@healtech.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Holt <sarah.holt@healtech.com>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 12:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data handling: retention scope and exception options (post-call recap)

Sarah — looping in a few specifics. Attaching a SOC 2 summary and a draft DPA with two proposed paths:
1) Hosted + DPA carve-outs: Redwood hosted API with documented route-based TTLs and a clause for on-demand preservation during investigations.
2) Private/Dedicated: VPC or private deployment for full data residency and isolation; retention controls can be enforced customer-side for strict zero-retention requirements.

Proposed sample retention matrix (high level) — we can formalize in the DPA: 
- Sensitive transcripts (tagged routes): 0-retention (no token logs, ephemeral KV)
- Non-sensitive transcripts: 24–72 hours
- User-facing KV cache: up to 7 days (configurable)
- Debug/tracing logs: 48 hours, preserved on-request if incident opened

Attachments (stubs):
- SOC2-summary.pdf (redwood redacted summary)
- DPA-proposed-redline.docx (tracks suggested clauses for route-based TTLs, on-demand preservation, and Private deployment option)

We can also include a short runbook in the DPA for how to request preservation and what logs are available. Let me know if you want a version that explicitly references PHI/PII controls for your legal team.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions Engineering — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

[Attachment placeholders: SOC2-summary.pdf, DPA-proposed-redline.docx]
From: Sarah Holt <sarah.holt@healtech.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: HealTech Legal <legal@healtech.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 10:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Data handling: retention scope and exception options (post-call recap)

Thanks Marcus — received the summary and draft DPA. HealTech legal reviewed the matrix and wants the following before we move to contracting: 
- A clear definition of what constitutes a "tagged sensitive route" and how tags are applied (api-key vs. route-level annotation).
- Confirmation that on-demand preservation requires a documented request and that only specific audit IDs will be preserved.
- Confirmation that Private deployment is available within 30 days of contract signature for our pilot flow.

We still prefer 0-retention for PHI flows; if Redwood can provide Private deployment as an option while we finalize DPA language, that would be ideal. Let's take the 11:00am ET sync as planned — I’ve invited our CISO and procurement and attached a short vendor-security-review.pdf for context.

Next steps (agreed):
- Redwood: provide a sentence-level definition for "tagged sensitive route" and confirm preservation workflow (Marcus to produce).
- HealTech: provide the legal team's redline after the call.
- Schedule: follow-up call Thurs 2/12 11:00am ET (30 min) — calendar invite sent.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — speak shortly.

Best,
Sarah
Head of Integrations, HealTech

Attachments referenced: vendor-security-review.pdf
